text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein reaffirms to Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat continuation of coordination to push forward Middle East peace process on all fronts.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti says any expansion of Jewish settlements would be considered a genuine destruction of the peace process.
- Kabariti says his government is committed to implementing a memorandum of understanding settling engineers' pay dispute after engineers stage three hour protest on Saturday.
- Zarqa mayor Mustafa al-Fayad released on bail.
- Jordan appeal court rules that Jordan's extradition treaty signed with the United States in 1995 is unconstitutional.
- Jordan Valley authorities finish study on issuing tender for technical study of planned Red Sea to Dead Sea canal.

- New customs tariffs to be implemented this week. Customs levy on cars to be cut to 40 percent, but will be compensated with other extra taxes. Cigarettes and drinks tariffs unchanged, maximum levels on all other goods to be 30-40 percent.
- Cabinet cancels minimum investment levels for foreigners in local projects and on stock exchange.
- Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai tells Jordan Times he is committed to strong ties with Jordan, ready to resolve bilateral problems.
